title: Fidelity Guardrails and Degradation Credit Framework for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a measurable SLA surface for Dedicated capacity that balances strict throughput guarantees with operationally realistic error-budgeting and an associated crediting mechanism that encourages graceful degradation instead of abrupt throttling.

Background: Customers on Dedicated want predictable serve rates for mission critical features but also need well-scoped remediation language that (a) limits our financial exposure, (b) preserves incentives to use autoscaling/fallbacks, and (c) avoids noisy short-window refunds for transient noise. Prior PM artifacts focus on fixed credit formulas; this work introduces a sliding-window fidelity guardrail and a tiered degradation-credit schedule tied to service fidelity and autoscale interlock behavior.

Scope: SLA metric definitions, measurement windows, credit calculation algorithm, contract clause drafts (plain-language + legal appendix snippets), monitoring & alerting requirements, autoscale interlock contract language, example calculations and customer-facing FAQ. Not in scope: billing system implementation details, final legal signoff language (legal to review), dedicated infra implementation PRs (linked as dependencies).

Acceptance criteria: 
- A single-page SLA spec that defines: Primary Serve Commitment metric, Acceptable Degradation band, and Error Budget windowing.
- A deterministic crediting formula with worked examples.
- Contract clause text for SOW + two short example contract snippets for typical mid-market and enterprise customers.
- An ops playbook describing detection, notification, mitigation ladder, and required runbook links.
- A list of implementation dependencies (Telemetry dashboard, autoscaler hooks, billing connector PR).
sla_spec:
Primary Serve Commitment: Committed Tokens/Minute (CTM) measured at customer account-level over a rolling 30-day window. CTM is defined as the 99th percentile of per-minute served tokens during business hours (customer-defined 8am-8pm local) aggregated across AZs.

Availability-Fidelity Band: We define three bands for each measurement window:
- Green: Served >= 100% of committed CTM (no remediation)
- Amber: Served between 90% and 99.99% of CTM (graceful degrade remediation applies; technical notification and playbook run)
- Red: Served < 90% of CTM (credits applicable per schedule)

Error Budget Windowing: 30-day rolling window with a per-day smoothing step using daily CTM floor to limit crediting sensitivity to single-day outages. The metric reported to contracts is the 30-day rolling percentile; credits calculated on the 30-day affected substantially below thresholds.
measurement_and_formulae:
Measurement pipeline: raw per-minute token counters -> dedupe by request id -> AZ-normalized ingestion -> compute per-minute served tokens -> compute 99th percentile over 30-day rolling window.

Credit calculation algorithm (plain formula):
If 30-day_percentile >= 100%: credit = $0
If 90% <= 30-day_percentile < 100%: credit = min(max_credit, base_credit * (1 - 30-day_percentile/100) * adjustment_factor)
If 30-day_percentile < 90%: credit = min(max_credit, escalation_credit + proportional_credit)

Where: base_credit = monthly committed fee * 0.05; max_credit = monthly committed fee * 0.50; escalation_credit = monthly committed fee * 0.10; adjustment_factor reduces credit if autoscale/alternative fallback was invoked successfully in >= 50% of amber windows.

Example: Customer commits to 1,000,000 tokens/min CTM; monthly committed fee = $45,000. 30-day percentile measured at 92%. Base credit = $2,250. Raw proportional = $2,250 * (1 - 0.92) = $180. If adjustment_factor = 0.8 (some fallback used), credit = $180 * 0.8 = $144 (capped by max_credit).
autoscale_and_interlock_policy:
Autoscale Interlock: When per-AZ queue depth crosses threshold T1 (configurable per pool), autoscaler enters 'pre-burst' mode and provisions additional reserved nodes up to pooled reserve. If autoscaler failed to provision due to capacity constraints and the failure contributed to sustained under-serve, reduction in credit may be eligible per adjustment_factor definition.

Burst Allowance: Customers receive a monthly burst allocation (BURST_TOKENS) set to 5% of committed throughput for masking short spikes (< 5 minutes). Bursts beyond that are subject to fair-share throttling but do not by themselves trigger crediting unless they contribute to the 30-day percentile falling below thresholds.

Graceful Degrade Requirements: SDK and API-level behavior must return structured fallback responses (503-with-hint or partial_response_token) so app teams can implement client-side degrade behavior. Contract requires customers to adopt a recommended fallback plan for enterprise SOWs to preserve higher credit caps.
contract_clauses_draft:
Draft plain-language clause (SLA Summary): 'Redwood commits to a dedicated serve rate of X tokens/min as specified on the order form (Committed Tokens/Minute, CTM). We measure CTM compliance on a rolling 30-day window using our standard telemetry. If the 30-day compliance falls below 90% we will issue credits up to 50% of the monthly committed fee as described in the Credit Schedule. For short-term degradations between 90% and 100% we will run our mitigation playbook and may issue smaller credits depending on autoscale and fallback usage.'

Legal appendix snippet: 'Credits are calculated using the rolling 30-day CTM percentile. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability-related failures under this SLA. Customer must open a support incident within 15 days of the end of the measurement window to be eligible for credits.'

Mid-market example paragraph (plain): 'For mid-market customers, credits will be applied automatically to the next invoice after telemetric verification. A 30-day remediation window applies during which Redwood and customer will collaborate on root-cause analysis.'
ops_playbook_and_alerting:
Detection: Alert when 30-day percentile drops below 101% (early-warning) and when it drops into Amber (>=90% <100%) and Red (<90%).

Notification ladder:
- T+0: Automatic alert to oncall + customer success + assigned SE (amber).
- T+6h: Activate mitigation playbook (verify autoscaler logs, check fallback invocations).
- T+24h: If still amber, open cross-functional incident and set customer expectation.
- T+72h: Escalate to Product & Eng leadership; evaluate temporary capacity shifts.

Required dashboards & runbooks: CTM 30-day rolling percentile (per-customer), per-AZ serve breakdown, autoscaler success/failure rate, fallback invocation ratio, billing credit ledger.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: 30-day smoothing reduces noisy refunds but delays remediation visibility for customers.
- Risk: Complex credit formulas create opacity; mitigate via worked examples in customer portal.
- Tradeoff: Tying credits to autoscaler/fallback behavior incentivizes customers to implement fallbacks but requires SDK/contract alignment.
- Risk: Burst pools add operational capacity overhead and complicate capacity planning.
